title: Install Sherpa handoff and blocker tally — Nov 2026
body:
Weekly notes: Install Sherpa & Handoff — Private Deploys (VPC + on-prem)
Date range: 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-08
Owner: Ava Chen (eng-private-deployments)
Objective: consolidate open blockers observed by field engineers, capture short-term workarounds, assign owners for final remediation, and prepare a lightweight handoff for customer success.

Attendees (standup cadence: Tue/Thu): Ava, Diego, Priya, Liam, Sara, Engineering on-call (rotation): Noor

Highlights / wins
- Helix Health: Completed day-2 validation of inference pods behind customer NLB; binary compatibility verified after driver pin applied — latency baseline within 8% of hosted numbers.
- New installer flag --skip-metrics-proxy added in PR #512 to allow installs into constrained networks while we work on long-lived proxy flow. Diego shipped quick test image.
- Customer handoff template updated with explicit post-install telemetry checklist (added to Confluence link above).

Current customer-facing blockers (high -> low)
1) Helix Health — KMS handshake intermittently fails when hardware firewall enforces TLS client certs. Observed 3 times in last 48h.
   - Symptom: installer stops at key-sync step, retry loop shows exponential backoff.
   - Triage notes: root cause likely TLS session resumption + client cert renegotiation with proxy in path. On call captured tcpdump and TLS logs (attached to JIRA-PDEP-1423).
   - Current workaround: manual certificate pin on firewall for customer KMS endpoint; restart installer. Works but requires security team approval.
   - Owner: Priya (short-term), Eng Cryptography (long-term) — ETA for permanent fix: 2 weeks.

2) BrightLane (edge retail) — KV cache warmup causing repeated cold-start latency spikes for first 50 queries after failover.
   - Symptom: 200–400ms p99 spikes on failover window (10–15s).
   - Triage notes: cache invalidation policy resets last-touch timestamps when node decommissions; on rejoin, prefix cache misses severe due to small warmup window and request fanout. Identified in JIRA-PDEP-1488.
   - Workaround: reduce post-failover routing fanout to single replica for 30s (applied via routing-policy override) — hammered into customer config.
   - Owner: Liam — long-term fix in serving-runtime cache manager to retain prefix snapshot across controlled failovers. Estimated patch + canary: 3 weeks.

3) Zenith (on-prem) — MTU mismatch across customer VPN + jumbo frames; intermittent gRPC stream resets increasing token latency.
   - Symptom: steady 0.5–1% error rate for streaming requests; observed packet fragmentation.
   - Workaround: installer now detects PMTU via trace and suggests disabling jumbo frames on hosts; field team scripted a quick check and restart.
   - Owner: Sara (field playbook update).

4) Several customers — ephemeral telemetry gaps after upgrade (missing request_id correlation for 30–90 minutes).
   - Root cause: metrics-proxy rollout defaulted to 100% immediate switch; new sampling agent drops trace headers during handover under load.
   - Workaround: roll back to previous proxy, or use --skip-metrics-proxy to install then manually enable staged rollout.
   - Owner: Diego + Observability (short-term). Tracker: internal Confluence incident note.

Operational notes / diagnostics learned this week
- New small-tool: install-sherpa inspect (WIP). CLI collects targeted artifacts (kube events, installer logs, metrics-proxy logs) and uploads to secure bucket; reduces noisy triage steps. Quick demo Thursday — PR coming.
- Log sample size matters: for KMS handshake, capturing 5 full TLS handshakes permitted us to correlate client hello extensions with firewall behavior. Remind field to enable capture flag before manual firewall changes.
- Install times: median successful on-prem install (with network quirks) is 17m; VPC installs average 9m. Keep these numbers in hand for CS communications.

Action items (owner, due)
- Priya: produce KMS-proof-of-concept for resilient handshake (TLS client cert caching / retry backoff tuning) — due 2026-11-22.
- Diego: land metrics-proxy staged rollout fix (preserve trace headers across handover) + small hotfix for --skip-metrics-proxy docs — due 2026-11-15.
- Liam: design cache snapshot mechanism for controlled failover (spec + perf test plan) — draft due 2026-11-18.
- Sara: update field playbook with PMTU detection script + quick remediation steps; push to shared drive and notify field — due 2026-11-12 (blocked by approvals).
- Ava: consolidate customer handoff checklist into a one-pager for CS that includes: minimal allowed firewall rules, MTU check, KMS cert expectations, and metrics verification steps — due 2026-11-13.

Open questions / risks
- KMS handshake fix may need product decision: allow customer-managed KMS endpoints to be white-labeled in our config or require ephemeral redirect. Security wants to avoid manual firewall exceptions.
- Cache snapshot persistence increases disk usage on nodes; need capacity estimates for typical 3–node clusters. Might affect Dedicated pricing if we must reserve local SSD.
- Installer --skip-metrics-proxy is a temporary escape hatch; long-term we should design an explicit degraded-mode UX that makes it safe for customers to operate without telemetry for short windows while preserving trace continuity.

Next steps / meeting cadence
- Continue Tue/Thu triage standups 09:30 PST with field and observability leads until the top 3 blockers are closed.
- Friday sync: handoff packet for Customer Success containing the final remediation steps for Helix and BrightLane.

Appendix: quick links and artifacts
- Confluence: Install Sherpa Checklist — https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PDEP/Install+Sherpa+Checklist
- JIRA: PDEP-1423 (KMS handshake), PDEP-1488 (KV cache warmup), PDEP-1510 (MTU detection script)
- GH: installer PR 512 (skip-metrics-proxy flag) — https://github.com/redwood-inference/installer/pull/512
- Note: artifacts (pcap, installer logs) uploaded to secure bucket; field has shortened urls in JIRA tickets.

Notes to self:
- When documenting workarounds, include security impact line to avoid ambiguous instructions for CS teams.
- Create a small demo video (2–3 min) showing PMTU detection script and the restart flow; helps field adoption.

End of digest.
